description:
FILED s408 (Opus 5) by a probe while shipping #337 (the my-sub scope rename).

    my sub f { "L" }
    print eval "f()";
        perl: L      PCL: undef, $@ = "Undefined subroutine &main::f called"

perl finds a lexical sub in the enclosing PAD, exactly as a string eval finds
an enclosing `my` VARIABLE.  PCL's eval capture alist (_eval_lexical_alist ->
p-eval's (list (cons "$x" $x) ...)) carries VARIABLES only, so the eval string
compiles `f()` against the package stash -- where a lexical sub is, correctly,
not present since #337 gave it a scope-unique name.

NOT A REGRESSION IN ANY MEANINGFUL SENSE, but be precise about it: before #337
this "worked" because EVERY lexical sub was also a package sub -- the same
accident that made two same-named ones clobber each other (#337 core).  The
failure is LOUD and trappable, never a wrong value.  Registered in
docs/not-supported.md, section "A lexical sub (my sub NAME) reached from a
place that is not the token stream".

POPULATION: unknown, believed ~zero outside t/op/lexsub.t (#341).  MEASURE
FIRST -- the shape is `eval "..."` mentioning a name a `my sub` declares in the
same file; grep both populations before designing anything.

FIX SHAPE (sized, not designed): the eval request would carry a SUB capture
alist alongside the variable one -- (name -> the renamed CL symbol) for every
lexical sub whose region covers the eval site -- and eval-mode name resolution
would consult it before the package stash.  That is the same seam #364
(string-eval feature inheritance) rides on: presumed state that must ride the
request AND key the eval cache (s387: a capture-dependent EMISSION must key the
cache, and eval-mode compiling happens in the pl2cl --server subprocess).  So
size it WITH #364, not before it.

BAR: name resolution => the full sweep is the gate (the s386/#296 rule).
subject: A STRING eval cannot see a lexical sub (`my sub f {…}; eval "f()"`) — the capture alist carries variables only; size with #364
